description: Doenjang Jjigae is a beloved Korean soybean paste stew, cherished for its deep, savory flavor and comforting warmth. This hearty dish combines fermented soybean paste with an array of vegetables, tofu, and sometimes meat or seafood, simmered to perfection. It is a staple in Korean households, often served bubbling hot as a side dish or a main course with rice.

ingredients.notes: Korean soybean paste, adjust to taste
Korean chili paste, optional for heat

instructions.title: Prepare the Stock and Vegetables
instructions.text: Dice the onion, zucchini, and potatoes. Slice the mushrooms and green chili peppers. Cube the firm tofu. If using anchovy stock, prepare it by boiling dried anchovies and kelp in water for 15 minutes, then straining to remove solids.

instructions.title: Combine Paste and Liquid Base
instructions.text: In a dolsot (Korean stone pot) or a medium pot, add the water or prepared anchovy stock. Stir in the doenjang until it is fully dissolved. For a spicier stew, incorporate the optional gochujang at this stage.

instructions.title: Add Base Vegetables and Simmer
instructions.text: Bring the doenjang mixture to a boil over medium-high heat. Add the diced onion, potato, and minced garlic to the pot. Reduce the heat to medium and allow it to simmer for about 10 minutes, or until the potatoes begin to soften.

instructions.title: Incorporate Main Ingredients
instructions.text: Add the zucchini, mushrooms, and any optional protein such as thinly sliced pork belly, beef brisket, or seafood like clams or shrimp. Continue to simmer the stew for an additional 5-7 minutes, ensuring all ingredients are cooking evenly.

instructions.title: Add Tofu and Peppers
instructions.text: Gently add the cubed firm tofu and the sliced green chili peppers to the pot. Simmer for an additional 3-5 minutes, allowing all the distinct flavors to meld together and the tofu to heat through completely.

instructions.title: Garnish and Serve Hot
instructions.text: Taste the stew and adjust seasoning if necessary, adding more doenjang or a pinch of salt if desired. Garnish generously with the chopped scallions just before serving. Serve the bubbling hot Doenjang Jjigae immediately with a bowl of freshly cooked rice and various Korean banchan (side dishes).

tips: For a deeper, more authentic flavor, always use homemade anchovy-kelp stock instead of plain water. The umami enhances the stew significantly.
The quality of your doenjang (Korean soybean paste) is paramount. Invest in a good quality, traditionally fermented paste as it forms the backbone of the stew's taste profile.
Doenjang Jjigae is best enjoyed bubbling hot, served directly from a dolsot (Korean stone pot) or a communal pot, accompanied by freshly steamed rice and an assortment of Korean banchan.
